subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput decision follow-up (FinPay)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: post-call recap + next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we have alignment:

Key points from the call:
- FinPay will be integrating LLM-powered fraud-detection assistants into your realtime payment flows.
- Primary concern: tail latency at peak (SLO target: 95th pctl < 120ms for inference) and sustained throughput (~1.2M tokens/min during peak batch windows).
- Secondary concerns: data isolation and audit logs for compliance, but initial focus is performance.

Options discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to get running, managed autoscaling, prefix caching. Might hit noisy-neighbor variability at 95th pctl depending on peak spike shape.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and isolation; easier to guarantee tail latency at scale.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): flagged as long-term if compliance requires on-prem keys/audit control.

Requested items (next steps):
1) Olivia/FinPay to confirm the realistic peak concurrency pattern (tokens/sec or requests/sec) and any hard latency SLOs beyond the 95th pctl noted above.
2) FinPay to share the short infra requirements doc you mentioned — we can run a quick sizing exercise and sample benchmark.
3) We'll produce a short comparison runbook (hosted vs dedicated) with expected latency/throughput ranges and cost estimates.

I attached a one-page template you can drop numbers into; if you can send the infra doc and a preferred time, Marissa and Rishi can run an internal sizing and follow up with recommended config.

Thanks — Neha

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finpay.com>

Cc: Alan Park <alan.park@finpay.com>, FinPay Engineering <eng-team@finpay.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: post-call recap + next steps

Thanks Neha — great summary. Quick answers: 

- Peak pattern: we have periodic settlement windows where we expect a 10–15 minute spike. During the spike we see ~2,000 requests/min with average payloads that map to about 600 tokens/request (so roughly 1.2M tokens/min as you said). Outside of that window, steady-state is ~50k tokens/min.
- Hard SLO: we'd like 95th pctl < 120ms, 99th pctl < 220ms max for customer-facing flows. For internal batch scoring flows higher latency (up to 400ms) is acceptable.
- Compliance: we can start with hosted for a PoC but want dedicated/isolated options for production if the latency numbers only meet targets with reserved capacity. Procurement (Alan) will need a cost/commitment view before we talk contracts.

Sending the infra doc now (attached). Can Marissa run a sizing + quick bench against our numbers and share recommendations? We're aiming to decide by Apr 15 so procurement can plan.

Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Product, FinPay
olivia.chen@finpay.com
Attachments: finpay-infra-reqs.pdf (attached)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finpay.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: post-call recap + next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks for the infra doc and the clear SLOs. I pulled together an initial sizing and notes from our runtime team (high level):

Initial assessment (based on 1.2M tokens/min during 10–15 minute spikes):
- Hosted API: would likely handle average loads easily; however, achieving consistent 95th < 120ms during concentrated spikes is risky due to multi-tenant variability unless we provision additional headroom. In practice, that means higher cost for hosted to reach the same tail latency as dedicated.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended for production if FinPay needs deterministic 95th pctl latency. A Dedicated pool with reserved GPU capacity + autoscaling buffer (small burst capacity) should meet 95th < 120ms and 99th < 220ms with good margin. We'll provide exact GPU counts in the sizing doc.
- Caching and batching: we can reduce effective tokens/min with prefix caching for repeated prompts and request batching for internal batch scoring (which will lower cost but only helps some flows).

Questions for you:
- During the spike, are requests uniformly distributed or do they come in short microbursts (multiple concurrent requests within seconds)? Microbursts push for lower queuing and more active workers.
- Are you open to a hybrid approach: Hosted for non-critical flows and a small Dedicated pool for customer-facing realtime flows? That often balances cost and performance.

Next steps I propose:
1) We'll run a microbench using your example payloads (can you confirm a small set of sample requests or synthetic generator?).
2) I'll share a short PDF with expected latency curves and a Dedicated sizing recommendation by EOD Tue Apr 6.
3) If that looks good, we can schedule a 30-min technical review with your infra team and procurement.

cc'ing Rishi for any kernel/quantization questions.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: post-call recap + next steps

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround. Olivia/Alan: can you send a 2–3 sample requests (real or redacted) and confirm whether the spike is microburst-y or smoothed over the 10–15 minutes? That will help Marissa target the bench.

If you prefer, we can do the hybrid approach Marissa suggested: start hosted for low-risk flows, spin up a small Dedicated pool for customer-facing realtime endpoints, then migrate fully to Dedicated if tails remain. I'll include estimated monthly committed costs in the sizing doc we share tomorrow so procurement has numbers for planning.

Proposed times for the 30-min technical review: Tue Apr 6 between 9–11am PT or Wed Apr 7 1–3pm PT. Which works for your infra team?

Next: attaching the benchmark template (runtimes-latency-bench.xlsx) — drop the samples in and Marissa will run tests.

Best — Neha
